title: Supporting Families of School-Aged Children With ADHD: A Dual-Generation Therapy Approach Through the BRIDGE Program
official: Supporting Families of School-Aged Children With ADHD: A Dual-Generation Therapy Approach Through the BRIDGE Program
summary: The present research study will evaluate the feasibility and preliminary efficacy of the adapted Building Regulation in Dual Generations program for families of children (8-12 years old) with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, creating the BRIDGE-ADHD program. The BRIDGE-ADHD program combines 10 weekly online psycho-education sessions with knowledge about ADHD and relevant parenting skills training videos to improve maternal wellbeing and parenting practices, thus supporting children's own psychological wellbeing through an intergenerational approach. This study will specifically evaluate whether the BRIDGE-ADHD program is able to reduce mothers' psychological distress (e.g., depression, anxiety, parenting stress) and simultaneously reduce their children's attention and/or behaviour problems.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Mothers must be 18 years old or older with both current and elevated symptoms of depression (T-score \> 5 on the PHQ-9).

  * Mothers must have a child between the ages of 8 and 12 years old.
  * Both mothers and children must currently live in Manitoba.
  * Mothers must self-report that their child has a diagnosis of ADHD. This will be confirmed by having mothers complete the CBCL (T-score \> 65) and through intake interviews with clinicians.
  * Both mothers and children must speak fluent English.
  * Mothers must have neither attempted suicide within the past year nor self-harmed resulting in an injury that either did or should have received medical attention within the past 6 months.

Exclusion Criteria:

* not meeting the listed criteria above
